source.facts: Confirmed by Winston (Nov 2026): co-founder and only designer; the other seven were developers; he made product calls and handed off designs; Nov 2022 – Jan 2025; A2–A4 sections are closest to v1.0 (iOS, Nov 2024; also on Android); live timing shipped and detected delays automatically from posted results; tournament mode exists because you don't need those features outside an event, other features help you find teams and tournaments then, and its UI is built for the fast-paced tournament environment (own experience + tester input); your own next match leads with the time because time is what you act on (own experience competing + user/team feedback); the 2023 plan's organizer portal, chatbot and web app gave way to priorities; the ScoutSheet tab (A5) shipped in a later update; TeamSync, Groups and the new onboarding (A5/R1/R2) were designed but not shipped; feedback after launch led to fixes only; 4,000+ accounts; 4.8-star rating; '3x faster' came from automated tests clicking through competitor apps vs Elapse to reach the same data. Takeaways he chose: design for the moment; ship the core first; live data needs honest states. Follow-up: live timing was in v1.0; tournament mode switches off after the event; some scouting (robot specs on the team sheet) was in v1.0.

fields.description: A tournament companion for VEX Robotics teams: next match, live schedule and scouting. 4,000+ accounts.
fields.intro: I co-founded Elapse, an app that shows VEX Robotics teams their next match, a live schedule and scouting. I was the only designer, working with seven developers.
fields.summary: How might we help robotics teams know when and where their next match is, even when the schedule runs late?
fields.overview: I made product calls and handed off designs to the developers. Elapse launched on iOS in November 2024 and is also on Android.

sections.title: Problem
sections.heading: Tournament day moves fast
content: I competed in VEX Robotics for four years. At tournaments, I ran into three problems:

bullets: The official schedule app took several taps and spread information across screens.
Schedules weren’t updated when matches ran late.
Announcements over the mic were easy to miss.

sections.title: Plan vs. release
sections.heading: From plan to release
content: The 2023 plan was bigger than what we launched. We cut it back because teams needed other things more, like scouting.

bullets: **Planned:** an organizer portal for delays and announcements, a chatbot, and a web app for phones, tablets and computers.
**Shipped in v1.0:** tournament mode, upcoming matches, live timing and basic scouting on each team’s sheet.
**Added later:** the ScoutSheet tab on each team’s page.
**Designed, not shipped:** team sharing and an onboarding flow.

sections.title: Next match
sections.heading: Your next match comes first
content: On your own next match, the time and “In X minutes” come first. Other matches lead with the match number.

bullets: **Why time first:** time is what you act on.
**Where it came from:** my own time competing, plus user and team feedback.

content.alt: Three iPhones: the Elapse home with a next match card, your next match leading with the time, and another match leading with the match number
content.caption: Home, your next match (time first), another match (number first).

sections.title: Live timing
sections.heading: Delays you can see
content: Matches often run late. Live timing worked out delays from posted match results and updated the schedule automatically.
Instead of quietly changing the time, the app shows the new time with “Delayed - originally …”, and finished matches show how late they started.

content.alt: Two iPhones: Your Next Match with “Delayed - originally” under the new time, and a finished match that started 3 minutes late
content.caption: A delayed match, and a finished one that started late.

sections.title: Tournament mode
sections.heading: A mode for tournament day
content: Tournament mode is for when you’re at an event. You turn it on from the home screen, and it switches off after the event.

bullets: **You don’t need it outside an event.** Other features help you find teams and tournaments then.
**Its UI is built for a fast-paced day** at the event.
**It came from my own experience** and from testers.

content.alt: Three iPhones: the Elapse home outside tournament mode with a Tournament Mode button, rankings opened as a separate screen, and rankings in the Tournament tab
content.caption: Turning it on from home, and rankings outside vs. inside tournament mode.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.heading: After launch
content: Elapse reached 4,000+ accounts with a 4.8-star rating. In our automated tests, which clicked through competitor apps and Elapse to reach the same data, Elapse was 3x faster. After launch, feedback led to fixes, not design changes.
The ScoutSheet tab on each team’s page came in a later update.

content.alt: Two iPhones: an Elapse team page with an empty Scoutsheet tab, and a filled ScoutSheet
content.caption: A team’s ScoutSheet, empty and filled.

bullets: **Design for the moment.** Tournament day leaves little attention. The next match has to be readable at a glance.
**Ship the core first.** Leaving the portal and chatbot out let us release what teams needed.
**Live data needs honest states.** Show a delay next to the original time instead of hiding it.
